answer: Sequential Work Ledger. Each identity must complete a proof-of-work chain signed with a hardware-rooted key, and every new identity must extend an existing chain's copper-anchored timestamp log. A single thread of verified computation therefore gates registration. Registering N sybils costs N times the median chain completion time plus hardware attestation, making mass identity creation linearly expensive in real compute and device procurement rather than capital. An atlas of valid chains is maintained by peers, so forks are rejected.
